pages.text:
Tuning: What to Correct and What to Leave 
 Tuning: What to Correct and What to Leave
 Figure 1. No correction, partial, and full. The bottom one is in tune and no longer sounds like a person.
 These are the controls this module turns on. Know what each one does before you decide what to set it to.
 Each control and what it does
 Control What it does 
 Correction amount How far the note moves toward the target pitch. Full correction is an effect, not a repair. 
 Correction speed How fast it gets there. Fast speeds remove the scoop into a note, which is often the performance. 
 Scale and key Constrains the target notes. Set it wrong and the corrector fights the singer. 
 Vibrato handling Vibrato is pitch modulation. Aggressive correction flattens it and the voice loses life. 
 Formant preservation Keeps the voice sounding like the same person when the pitch moves. 
 Figure 2. The correction pulls the pitch toward the note and leaves the shape of the phrase alone. Flatten the shape too and it stops sounding sung.

pages.title: Dynamic Effects: Compression, The Seven Controls
pages.text:
Dynamic Effects: Compression, The Seven Controls 
 Dynamic Effects: Compression, The Seven Controls
 Figure 1. Six rules worth having in your head before you touch a single control.
 Seven controls, one question. Threshold, ratio, attack, release, knee, makeup and side-chain all exist to answer one thing: what should this track do when it gets loud. Decide that first and the settings follow.
 Figure 2. The Dyn3 Compressor and Limiter panel. Ratio, Threshold, Attack, Knee, Release, Depth and Gain are the seven controls every compression decision comes down to.
 These are the controls this module turns on. Know what each one does before you decide what to set it to.
 Each control and what it does
 Control What it does 
 Threshold The level above which compression happens. Everything else is a response to this. 
 Ratio How hard it compresses above threshold. 2:1 is gentle shaping, 10:1 and above is limiting. 
 Attack How fast it clamps down. Fast attack catches the transient, slow attack lets it through. 
 Release How fast it lets go. Too fast pumps, too slow and the next note arrives still compressed. 
 Knee How abruptly the ratio engages around the threshold. Soft knee for transparency, hard knee for control. 
 Makeup gain Puts back what compression took. Always compare at matched loudness. 
 Gain reduction meter The only control that tells you the truth. Watch it more than you watch the knobs. 
 A fast attack is not a safe default. Attack times under about 3 ms clamp the transient, which is the part that tells a listener a drum was hit. If the kick went soft after you patched the compressor in, the attack is too fast.
 Set release by the tempo. Let the gain reduction meter return to zero just before the next hit. If the needle never comes back, the release is too slow and the track is being held down continuously instead of being shaped.
 Figure 3. The same compressor on the same source. Above, no side chain filter and the kick drives the whole gain reduction. Below, a high pass at 100 Hz on the detector and the pumping is gone.

pages.title: Dynamic Effects: Common Mistakes and How to Hear Them
pages.text:
Dynamic Effects: Common Mistakes and How to Hear Them 
 Dynamic Effects: Common Mistakes and How to Hear Them
 These are the errors that cost marks. Every item below has shown up in real student submissions in this course. Read them before you submit, not after you get the grade back.
 Figure 1. The same drum hit with a slow and a fast attack. The flattened spike on the lower waveform is the punch you just gave away.
 Every one of these is a mistake that gets made in this room every semester. The middle column is the part worth memorizing: what the mistake sounds like is how you catch it in your own work.
 Each mistake, the sound that gives it away, and what to do instead
 The mistake What you hear What to do instead 
 Setting attack too fast on drums The kick loses its front end and the mix loses its punch. Slow the attack until the transient comes back, then set the release by the groove. 
 Judging compression at a louder level Everything compressed sounds better because it is louder. Match the makeup gain so bypassed and engaged are the same loudness, then decide. 
 Compressing to a number A ratio and a threshold that look right on paper and do nothing for the track. Watch the gain reduction meter and listen to what is moving. 3 dB on the right thing beats 10 dB on the wrong thing. 
 Hearing it is the skill. Each mistake has a listening cue attached. Learn the cue and you stop needing the checklist.

pages.title: Spectral Effects and EQ: Why We Use Equalization
pages.text:
Spectral Effects and EQ: Why We Use Equalization 
 Spectral Effects and EQ: Why We Use Equalization
 EQ is a decision, not a habit. Every move you make should answer a question you asked first. "The vocal is buried" is a question. "I always high-pass at 80" is a habit.
 Figure 1. The 304E Equalizer. Bass, Mid and Treble with a sweepable Mid Frequency, which is enough to hear what a broad tonal move does before reaching for a surgical filter.
 Equalization, often shortened to EQ, is the process of changing the level of specific frequency ranges in audio so that the sound is clearer, more balanced, and more appropriate for the listening context.
 Core Reasons We EQ
 We EQ to improve clarity by reducing frequency buildup that masks important detail in a voice, instrument, or mix.
 We EQ to shape tone by emphasizing or softening parts of the spectrum that influence how something feels, such as warmth, presence, or brightness.
 We EQ to solve problems by reducing resonances, harshness, rumble, or boomy frequencies that distract from the intended sound.
 We EQ to make multiple tracks fit together by carving space so each element can be heard without competing in the same frequency range.
 We EQ to match a target by adjusting a recording or mix so it translates better across different playback systems, rooms, and listeners.
 EQ Goals in Plain Language
 We EQ to remove what is not helping the sound.
 We EQ to highlight what matters most in the sound.
 We EQ to help the listener understand and emotionally connect with what they are hearing.
 Two Common EQ Approaches
 Corrective EQ focuses on fixing issues like boxiness, muddiness, harshness, hum, rumble, and resonant ringing.
 Tonal EQ focuses on shaping character, such as adding warmth, adding presence, or smoothing brightness for a more polished sound.
 When EQ Is Not the Best First Move
 If the source is wrong, we often get better results by changing the instrument, the player, the microphone choice, or the microphone placement.
 If the room is causing problems, we often get better results by changing the position in the room, adding absorption, or reducing reflective surfaces.
 If the level balance is off, we often get better results by adjusting faders before reaching for EQ.
 Interactive Parametric EQ Reference
 Use this interactive tool to explore how a parametric equalizer affects the sound, including frequency, gain, and Q (bandwidth).
 Interactive Parametric EQ Tool (Webtet) 
 Cut before you boost. Cutting the frequency that is in the way costs no headroom and changes no tone anywhere else. Boosting the frequency you want raises the whole track and usually needs the fader pulled back anyway.
 Do not EQ in solo. A track soloed has nothing to be masked by, so every problem you hear in solo is a problem that may not exist in the mix. Judge the move in context, every time.
 Figure 2. Left, both sources fight for the same band and the sum goes muddy. Right, one is cut where the other lives, and both are audible.

pages.title: Spectral Effects and EQ: Filter Shapes and What They Are For
pages.text:
Spectral Effects and EQ: Filter Shapes and What They Are For 
 Spectral Effects and EQ: Filter Shapes and What They Are For
 The shape is the decision. A bell fixes one problem. A shelf changes a whole region. A high-pass removes what was never wanted. Picking the wrong shape is a bigger error than picking the wrong frequency.
 Figure 1. The 304E Equalizer. Bass, Mid and Treble with a sweepable Mid Frequency, which is enough to hear what a broad tonal move does before reaching for a surgical filter.
 These are the controls this module turns on. Know what each one does before you decide what to set it to.
 Each control and what it does
 Control What it does 
 High-pass filter Removes energy below a corner frequency. The most useful filter in a mix and the easiest to overuse. 
 Low shelf Lifts or cuts everything below a frequency by a fixed amount. Broad tonal shaping. 
 Bell, or peaking Boosts or cuts around a center frequency. Q sets how wide. 
 Q Narrow Q for surgical cuts, wide Q for musical shaping. A narrow boost almost always sounds worse than a wide one. 
 High shelf Air and presence, or the opposite. Gentler than a bell for top-end work. 
 High-pass with your eyes shut. Sweep the high-pass up until the track thins, then back it off until it is full again. The point where it thinned is what the track actually needed, not 80 Hz because that is the number everyone repeats.
 Narrow Q is for problems, not for tone. A Q above about 4 is a scalpel for a resonance or a ring. Using it to shape tone leaves a notch that follows the track through every arrangement change and sounds wrong on half of them.
 Figure 2. Boost wide, cut narrow. A broad lift sounds like tone. A narrow notch sounds like a problem being removed, which is what you want it to sound like.

items.stem: A vocal jumps in level from line to line and never quite sits with the band. A student sends it to a hall reverb to glue it in. What should they do first?
options: Fix the dry vocal level before adding reverb
Lengthen the decay so the tail covers the jumps
Give the vocal its own reverb on an insert
Raise the pre-delay so the quiet lines stand out
key: Fix the dry vocal level before adding reverb
items.title: Question

items.stem: Two acoustic guitars sit at the same level and both feel right up front. You want one of them to sit further back in the room while keeping its level about where it is. Which move does that?
options: Raise its send to the shared reverb
Add more pre-delay to its reverb
Boost a high shelf on it for more air
Pan it to the center behind the vocal
key: Raise its send to the shared reverb
items.title: Question

items.stem: A mix has a separate D-Verb inserted on each of eight tracks, and the whole thing has turned to mud. EQ on the reverbs has not helped. What fixes the underlying problem?
options: Replace them with one or two shared send reverbs
Shorten the decay on all eight by the same amount
Pan the eight reverbs to different positions
Lower the wet mix on each insert by the same amount
key: Replace them with one or two shared send reverbs
items.title: Question

items.stem: D-Verb sits on an aux return fed by sends from several tracks. How do you set the plugin wet and dry mix?
options: Fully wet, and use each send level to set how much reverb each track gets
Halfway, so each track gets an even blend of dry and wet
Mostly dry, so the reverb cannot overwhelm the tracks
Different on every song section, automated to follow the arrangement
key: Fully wet, and use each send level to set how much reverb each track gets
items.title: Question

items.stem: What can help you visualize the kind of space you want the blended sounds to inhabit?
options: Closing your eyes
Using only default presets
Reading the manual
Increasing the reverb tail
key: Closing your eyes
items.title: Quiz 11_Balancing and Reverb

items.stem: Why is it important to check the effect in mono when using reverb?
options: To prevent nasty tonal changes
To ensure volume balance
To enhance dynamic characteristics
To prevent audience immersion
key: To prevent nasty tonal changes
items.title: Quiz 11_Balancing and Reverb

items.stem: What should you do to better hear the reverb decay?
options: Mute and un-mute the track
Use a different plug-in
Increase the volume
Adjust the frequency balance
key: Mute and un-mute the track
items.title: Quiz 11_Balancing and Reverb

items.stem: What is one reason you might want to use a second blend reverb with less pre-delay?
options: To reduce masking of the wet signal by the dry signal
To add more low frequencies
To increase the stereo spread
To enhance the brightness of the sound
key: To reduce masking of the wet signal by the dry signal
items.title: Quiz 11_Balancing and Reverb

pages.title: Balancing and Reverb: Procedure Guide
pages.text:
Balancing and Reverb: Procedure Guide 
 Balancing and Reverb: Procedure Guide
 Follow this in order. Each step assumes the one before it is complete. If a step will not work, the cause is almost always something skipped earlier, not the step you are on.
 Figure 1. D-Verb, with all seven algorithms visible. Note there is no early reflections control: pre-delay, decay, diffusion and HF cut are what you actually shape a space with here.
 Use this self-contained guide before completing the assignment work in this module. It explains the operating workflow; the corresponding assignment provides the required project-specific settings and submission evidence.
 Step-by-Step Workflow
 Establish the dry balance first. Do not use reverb to hide an unresolved fader, pan, timing, or EQ problem.
 Create an aux return with the reverb inserted and send tracks to it from their send controls rather than inserting separate reverbs on every source.
 Set pre-delay, decay, damping, and return level to support the song tempo and depth without obscuring articulation.
 Automate send or return level only after the static reverb balance works, then verify the mix in mono and at a low listening level.
 Reference: Apply the current Avid Pro Tools Reference Guide procedures that correspond to the tools used here. Keep an untouched playlist or session version before making destructive edits. 
 This page is self-contained and does not rely on links to other Canvas pages.
 Save before and after. Save the session before you start and again when you finish, with a version number in the name. It costs two seconds and it is the only undo that survives a crash.

pages.title: Balancing and Reverb: Placing a Source in a Space
pages.text:
Balancing and Reverb: Placing a Source in a Space 
 Balancing and Reverb: Placing a Source in a Space
 What reverb is actually for. Reverb does not make a track sound better. It puts the track somewhere. Before you open D-Verb, decide how far back this source should sit and whether it belongs in the same room as everything else.
 Figure 1. D-Verb, with all seven algorithms visible. Note there is no early reflections control: pre-delay, decay, diffusion and HF cut are what you actually shape a space with here.
 These are the controls this module turns on. Know what each one does before you decide what to set it to.
 Each control and what it does
 Control What it does 
 Algorithm Hall, Church, Plate, Room, Ambient, Non-Linear. Each is a different assumption about the space. 
 Pre-delay The gap before the reverb arrives. Longer pre-delay keeps the source forward while still placing it. 
 Decay How long the tail lasts. Match it to the tempo, not to taste. 
 Diffusion How quickly the reflections smear together. Low diffusion is discrete echoes, high is a wash. 
 Wet and dry balance On a send, this stays fully wet and the send level does the work. 
 Set decay to the tempo, not to taste. Play the song and lengthen decay until the tail just clears before the next downbeat. At 120 BPM that is roughly 1.8 seconds. Longer than that and the tail sits on top of the next chord.
 One reverb per source is how a mix turns to mud. Use one or two send reverbs the whole mix shares. Eight instances of D-Verb on eight inserts is eight different rooms fighting each other, and no amount of EQ fixes that.
 Figure 2. Bigger room, longer pre delay and longer decay. Pick the space first, then set the two numbers to match it.

pages.title: Balancing & Reverb: Common Mistakes and How to Hear Them
pages.text:
Balancing & Reverb: Common Mistakes and How to Hear Them 
 Balancing & Reverb: Common Mistakes and How to Hear Them
 These are the errors that cost marks. Every item below has shown up in real student submissions in this course. Read them before you submit, not after you get the grade back.
 Figure 1. Reverb on an insert against reverb on a send. The send version gives you one space, many sources, and one fader to control it.
 Every one of these is a mistake that gets made in this room every semester. The middle column is the part worth memorizing: what the mistake sounds like is how you catch it in your own work.
 Each mistake, the sound that gives it away, and what to do instead
 The mistake What you hear What to do instead 
 Reverb on an insert instead of a send You cannot share the space, you cannot balance it, and the dry signal is stuck to it. Put reverb on a send and return. One space, many sources, one fader to control it. 
 No pre-delay The source moves backward in the mix and loses its front. Add 20 to 40 ms and hear the source step forward while staying in the space. 
 Decay that fights the tempo The tail is still going when the next chord arrives and the mix is mud. Set decay by ear against the tempo, then shorten it until the mix breathes. 
 Hearing it is the skill. Each mistake has a listening cue attached. Learn the cue and you stop needing the checklist.

items.stem: What are the benefits of using delay effects over reverb in audio mixing?
options: Delay effects provide more control over timing and rhythm.
Delay effects are easier to use than reverb.
Delay effects create a more natural sound environment.
Delay effects are more suitable for live performances.
key: Delay effects provide more control over timing and rhythm.
items.title: Quiz 12_Delay and Stereo Enhancements

items.stem: Describe the difference between a send-return effect configuration and an insert setup when using delay effects.
options: A send-return configuration allows for parallel processing of the delay effect, while an insert setup processes the effect in series with the original signal.
Both configurations process the effect in series with the original signal.
A send-return configuration processes the effect in series with the original signal, while an insert setup allows for parallel processing of the delay effect.
Both configurations allow for parallel processing of the delay effect.
key: A send-return configuration allows for parallel processing of the delay effect, while an insert setup processes the effect in series with the original signal.
items.title: Quiz 12_Delay and Stereo Enhancements

items.stem: What is a common problem when using a single 50 to 100ms short 'slapback' delay with little or no feedback?
options: It creates a muddy sound
It results in a thin sound
It causes phase cancellation
It introduces unwanted distortion
key: It creates a muddy sound
items.title: Quiz 12_Delay and Stereo Enhancements

items.stem: At 120 BPM a quarter note lasts 500 ms, an eighth note is half a quarter, and a dotted note lasts one and a half times its plain value. Your delay plugin has no tempo sync. What do you type in for a dotted eighth note delay?
options: 250 ms
375 ms
500 ms
750 ms
key: 375 ms
items.title: Question

items.stem: A straight eighth note delay on a busy vocal makes the line harder to follow, because every repeat lands on the next syllable. What does the module suggest trying before you give up on the delay?
options: More feedback, so the repeats blend together
A louder return, so the repeats read as intentional
A dotted eighth, which lands between the beats
A reverb, since delay does not suit dense vocals
key: A dotted eighth, which lands between the beats
items.title: Straight eighth crowds the vocal

items.stem: You want one delay shared by the vocal, the acoustic guitar and the piano, with a different amount of it on each. How do you set that up?
options: A copy of the delay inserted on each of the three tracks
One delay on an aux return, fed by a separate send from each track
The delay inserted on the vocal, with the other two routed through it
The delay inserted on the master buss, with the wet mix pulled back
key: One delay on an aux return, fed by a separate send from each track
items.title: One delay, three sources

items.stem: The delay return is already quieter than the vocal, but the repeats still pull your ear off the dry track. What does the module have you do to the return?
options: Raise the feedback so the repeats blur into each other
Boost the presence range on the return so it matches the vocal
Roll off the top and bottom of the return so the repeats sit behind
Pan the return hard to one side and leave the level alone
key: Roll off the top and bottom of the return so the repeats sit behind
items.title: Repeats still pull focus

items.stem: You sum the master to mono after a widening move. Select every result that means the move is taking more than it gives.
options: The low end drops
The stereo image collapses toward the center
The widened source gets quieter or thinner
The widened part disappears almost entirely
key: The low end drops
The widened source gets quieter or thinner
The widened part disappears almost entirely
items.title: Reading the mono check

items.stem: You add a delay to widen an acoustic guitar. Instead of reading as width it smears the guitar and blurs its attack. The return is panned to the same side as the dry track and the time is set to 120 ms. What do you change first?
options: Add feedback so the repeats fill in behind the guitar
Boost the top end of the return so the repeats cut through
Pan the return opposite the source and shorten the time to 15 to 30 ms
Raise the return level until the width becomes obvious
key: Pan the return opposite the source and shorten the time to 15 to 30 ms
items.title: Width delay that smears

items.stem: Two ways to widen a pad: a stereo imager that inverts the polarity of the side content, or a 20 ms delay panned opposite the source. Which one holds together better when the mix is summed to mono?
options: The imager, because it works on level rather than phase
The delay, because an offset in time mostly survives summing
Both equally, since mono summing only removes the panning
Neither, so width is always a stereo only decision
key: The delay, because an offset in time mostly survives summing
items.title: Imager versus delay in mono

items.stem: A student duplicates one guitar take onto a second track, pans the two copies hard left and hard right, and raises both faders. The guitar gets louder but no wider. Why?
options: The two hard pans cancel each other at the master buss
A duplicated track is automatically out of polarity with its source
Width comes from difference between the channels, and the sides are identical
The pans are right but the delay between the two sides is wrong
key: Width comes from difference between the channels, and the sides are identical
items.title: Copy panned hard both ways

items.stem: How does the module tell you to find the level for a delay return?
options: Match the return level to the level of the dry track and leave it
Leave the plugin wet and dry mix control at its halfway default
Raise it until clearly audible, then lower it until you notice it only when it stops
Set it so the return meter has only just started to move
key: Raise it until clearly audible, then lower it until you notice it only when it stops
items.title: Setting the return level

items.stem: Why does the procedure guide have you match loudness before comparing the bypassed and active delay?
options: Bypassing the plugin resets the delay time back to its default value
Louder almost always wins, so an unmatched comparison proves only which is louder
Plugin latency makes the bypassed signal arrive ahead of the processed one
The output meters will not read the same until the two levels match
key: Louder almost always wins, so an unmatched comparison proves only which is louder
items.title: Matched loudness bypass

items.stem: Your delay time is exactly on the grid, but against the drummer it sits stiff and fights the feel of the track. What does the module tell you to do?
options: Raise the feedback so the timing error gets buried in the repeats
Quantize the drums so that they agree with the delay timing
Switch to a reverb, since this tempo will not support a delay
Tap it against the track and keep a value slightly off the grid if it sits better
key: Tap it against the track and keep a value slightly off the grid if it sits better
items.title: On the grid, wrong feel

items.stem: Your delay sits on an aux return fed by a post fader send from the vocal. You pull the vocal fader down 3 dB for the verse. What happens to the repeats?
options: They stay where they were, so the delay becomes more prominent
They get louder, because more signal is left over for the aux
They drop with the fader, so the wet to dry ratio stays where you set it
Nothing changes until you reopen the send and reset its level
key: They drop with the fader, so the wet to dry ratio stays where you set it
items.title: Post fader send behavior

items.stem: Why is low frequency content the riskiest thing in a mix to widen?
options: Low frequencies cannot be panned in a DAW at all
Phase based width cancels in mono, and losing the lows costs the mix its weight
Low frequencies are omnidirectional, so widening them does nothing audible
Widening the lows always pushes the peak level into clipping
key: Phase based width cancels in mono, and losing the lows costs the mix its weight
items.title: Widening the low end

items.stem: The song has a tempo map and the bridge slows down. Your delay time was calculated for the verse tempo and typed into the plugin. What happens, and what is the fix?
options: Nothing happens, because millisecond values do not depend on tempo
The repeats get louder in the bridge, so pull the feedback down
The repeats drift off the beat in the bridge, so switch the plugin to tempo sync
The plugin doubles the time by itself, so halve the note value
key: The repeats drift off the beat in the bridge, so switch the plugin to tempo sync
items.title: Typed time against a tempo map

pages.title: Delay and Stereo Enhancements: Width Without Losing Mono
pages.text:
Delay and Stereo Enhancements: Width Without Losing Mono 
 Delay and Stereo Enhancements: Width Without Losing Mono
 Width is a trade, not a gift. Every widening trick works by making the two channels different. The more different they are, the more cancels when someone plays the mix on one speaker, which is most phones, most club systems and every laptop.
 Figure 1. The Moogerfooger Analog Delay. Delay Time, Feedback and Mix are the three that set whether a delay supports the part or competes with it.
 These are the controls this module turns on. Know what each one does before you decide what to set it to.
 Each control and what it does
 Control What it does 
 Delay time Set against tempo. A quarter, an eighth or a dotted eighth are starting points, not rules. 
 Feedback How many repeats. More than a few and you are building a texture, not an effect. 
 Filtering in the repeats Darker repeats sit behind the source. Full-range repeats compete with it. 
 Stereo spread Difference between the channels. Real width comes from difference, not from level. 
 Mono compatibility Whatever you do to widen, check it summed. Phase tricks that vanish in mono are not width, they are a gamble. 
 Check mono before you commit. Sum the master to mono and listen. If the widened part vanishes or the low end drops, the trick is stealing more than it gives. Narrow it until mono survives.
 Delay beats a stereo plugin for width. A 15 to 30 ms delay on one side reads as width and mostly survives mono. A stereo imager that phase-inverts the sides does not.
 Figure 2. The side signal is two lobes of opposite polarity with a null between them. Anything arriving on that plane is centre, and disappears from the side channel entirely.

pages.title: Delay & Stereo Enhancements: Common Mistakes and How to Hear Them
pages.text:
Delay & Stereo Enhancements: Common Mistakes and How to Hear Them 
 Delay & Stereo Enhancements: Common Mistakes and How to Hear Them
 These are the errors that cost marks. Every item below has shown up in real student submissions in this course. Read them before you submit, not after you get the grade back.
 Figure 1. A wide stereo image and the same content summed to mono. Width built on phase difference is width you lose the moment anyone plays it on one speaker.
 Every one of these is a mistake that gets made in this room every semester. The middle column is the part worth memorizing: what the mistake sounds like is how you catch it in your own work.
 Each mistake, the sound that gives it away, and what to do instead
 The mistake What you hear What to do instead 
 Widening with a phase trick Wide and impressive in stereo, thin or absent in mono. Check mono before you commit. If it collapses, find the width another way. 
 Delay repeats as loud as the source The delay competes with the part instead of supporting it. Pull the return down until you notice it only when it stops. 
 Delay time set by eye Technically on the grid and rhythmically wrong. Tap it against the track. A delay slightly off the grid often sits better than one on it. 
 Hearing it is the skill. Each mistake has a listening cue attached. Learn the cue and you stop needing the checklist.

items.stem: Aliasing is:  (mark all that apply)
options: A type of distortion caused by digitally recording a signal at a lower sample rate than it should be
A good way to make a signal sound like an old video game
Creates a metallic edge to a sound
Adds information to the signal that is harmonically related to the original signal
key: A type of distortion caused by digitally recording a signal at a lower sample rate than it should be
A good way to make a signal sound like an old video game
Creates a metallic edge to a sound
items.title: Quiz_13_Distortion

items.stem: What is a subharmonic synthesizer?
options: An effect that adds low frequency energy to a signal that is still musically related to the unprocessed sound
An effect that adds low frequency information to a signal similar to an EQ boost
An effect that adds high frequency information to a signal that psychoacoustically tricks your brain into thinking a pitch is lower than it actually is
key: An effect that adds low frequency energy to a signal that is still musically related to the unprocessed sound
items.title: Quiz_13_Distortion

items.stem: Clipping is always a bad thing.
options: True
False
key: False
items.title: Quiz_13_Distortion

items.stem: Distortion is the addition or loss of information from the original signal.
options: True
False
key: True
items.title: Quiz_13_Distortion

items.stem: You can add gain to a signal forever without any change to the quality of the original signal.
options: True
False
key: False
items.title: Quiz_13_Distortion

items.stem: When adding harmonic distortion to a signal, be aware that you are adding extra harmonic information to the signal below the fundamental.
options: True
False
key: False
items.title: Quiz_13_Distortion

items.stem: One way to make use of the added high frequency information in a distorted signal is to use an EQ after the distortion to funnel the added spectral energy into those areas where it's really needed.
options: True
False
key: True
items.title: Quiz_13_Distortion

items.stem: You A/B a saturated bass against the dry signal and the saturated one sounds better. What must you check before trusting that?
options: That the master fader is at unity
That both are at matched loudness, because saturation raises perceived level
That the session sample rate has not changed
That the saturation plugin is in mono
key: That both are at matched loudness, because saturation raises perceived level
items.title: Effects: Quiz - Distortion

items.stem: What is the audible difference between soft clipping and hard clipping?
options: Soft clipping is inaudible and hard clipping is audible
Soft clipping raises level and hard clipping lowers it
Soft clipping only affects low frequencies
Soft clipping rounds the peaks and adds mostly lower order harmonics, hard clipping squares them and adds harsh upper harmonics
key: Soft clipping rounds the peaks and adds mostly lower order harmonics, hard clipping squares them and adds harsh upper harmonics
items.title: Effects: Quiz - Distortion

items.stem: You want a bass to read on small speakers that cannot reproduce its fundamental. What does saturation give you?
options: Harmonics above the fundamental that imply the pitch the speaker cannot produce
A boost to the fundamental itself
A reduction in the dynamic range of the part
A wider stereo image for the bass
key: Harmonics above the fundamental that imply the pitch the speaker cannot produce
items.title: Effects: Quiz - Distortion

items.stem: What distinguishes even order harmonics from odd order harmonics in how they sound?
options: Even order tends to sound warm and musical, odd order tends to sound aggressive or harsh
Even order is always inaudible, odd order is always audible
Even order raises level, odd order lowers it
Even order affects only the top octave
key: Even order tends to sound warm and musical, odd order tends to sound aggressive or harsh
items.title: Effects: Quiz - Distortion

items.stem: A drum buss sounds lifeless after heavy compression. Why might light saturation help more than more compression?
options: It lowers the noise floor of the buss
It widens the stereo image of the drums
It adds harmonic content and apparent loudness without further reducing dynamics
It restores the transients that compression removed
key: It adds harmonic content and apparent loudness without further reducing dynamics
items.title: Effects: Quiz - Distortion

items.stem: What is the most common mistake when using a distortion plugin on a full mix?
options: Setting the output level too low
Driving it hard enough that the low end loses definition and the top becomes harsh
Placing it before the master fader
Using it in mono rather than stereo
key: Driving it hard enough that the low end loses definition and the top becomes harsh
items.title: Effects: Quiz - Distortion

items.stem: Why does parallel distortion often work better than inserting distortion directly?
options: Parallel routing avoids phase problems entirely
Parallel routing increases the sample rate
The dry signal keeps its transients and dynamics while the distorted signal adds weight
Parallel routing uses less CPU
key: The dry signal keeps its transients and dynamics while the distorted signal adds weight
items.title: Effects: Quiz - Distortion

items.stem: Input drive and output level are set independently. Why does that matter when you judge the result?
options: Drive and output do the same thing at different resolutions
Output drive introduces latency and input drive does not
Only output level affects the harmonic content
Drive changes the character, output only changes level, and louder always sounds better
key: Drive changes the character, output only changes level, and louder always sounds better
items.title: Effects: Quiz - Distortion

items.stem: What does tape saturation do to transients that clean gain does not?
options: It softens and rounds them, reducing peak level while keeping apparent loudness
It sharpens them and increases peak level
It leaves them unchanged and only adds noise
It delays them relative to the rest of the signal
key: It softens and rounds them, reducing peak level while keeping apparent loudness
items.title: Effects: Quiz - Distortion

items.stem: Where in the chain would you place distortion intended to add weight to a bass part?
options: Before any EQ so the distortion shapes the raw signal
After the master fader for the whole mix
On the reverb return only
After corrective EQ so you are distorting the tone you actually want
key: After corrective EQ so you are distorting the tone you actually want
items.title: Effects: Quiz - Distortion

items.stem: A distorted guitar sounds fine alone and disappears in the mix. What is a likely cause?
options: The distortion filled the midrange with harmonics that other parts are masking
The distortion removed the guitar's fundamental entirely
The guitar is out of polarity with itself
The distortion lowered its overall level
key: The distortion filled the midrange with harmonics that other parts are masking
items.title: Effects: Quiz - Distortion

items.stem: Why does distortion make a source seem louder even when the meter reading has not changed?
options: Distortion shifts the source forward in the stereo field
Distortion lowers the noise floor so more detail is audible
Added harmonics increase perceived loudness without raising peak level
Distortion raises the peak level but not the meter reading
key: Added harmonics increase perceived loudness without raising peak level
items.title: Effects: Quiz - Distortion

items.stem: What should you listen for to know distortion has gone too far on a vocal?
options: The vocal moving to one side of the stereo image
The vocal level dropping below the instruments
The reverb tail shortening
Sibilance turning harsh and the consonants becoming brittle
key: Sibilance turning harsh and the consonants becoming brittle

items.stem: What is clip gain used for that a distortion plugin is not?
options: Adding harmonic content to a dull source
Softening transients on a drum buss
Widening the stereo image
Correcting level before the signal reaches any processing
key: Correcting level before the signal reaches any processing
items.title: Effects: Quiz - Distortion

items.stem: Heavily distorting the low end of a mix causes what specific problem?
options: The low end moves to the right of the stereo field
The low end drops below the noise floor
Harmonics in the low mids muddy the mix and the bass loses definition
The bass shifts out of polarity with the kick
key: Harmonics in the low mids muddy the mix and the bass loses definition
items.title: Effects: Quiz - Distortion

items.stem: You need a source to cut through without raising its level. Which is the better first move and why?
options: A wide low shelf boost, because it adds weight
A longer reverb, because it adds size
Hard limiting, because it raises the average level
Light saturation, because the added harmonics sit where small speakers and ears are most sensitive
key: Light saturation, because the added harmonics sit where small speakers and ears are most sensitive

pages.title: Mixing: Master-Buss Processing & Endgame: Module Overview
pages.text:
Mixing: Master-Buss Processing & Endgame: Module Overview 
 Mixing: Master-Buss Processing & Endgame
 Figure 1. Everything arrives here. What you do on the master buss affects all of it at once, which is the reason to do very little.
 Figure 2. Channel Strip, showing the EQ curve and the dynamics graph in one window. On a master buss every move here should be small enough to argue for.
 Learning Objectives
 Apply master buss processing in small, defensible amounts
 Use automation to serve the arrangement rather than fix it
 Deliver a mix at the correct level and headroom
 Before Class
 Master-Buss Processing and Endgame: Procedure Guide 
 Conclusion
 Work through the material above, then complete the graded work for this module.
 Effects: Quiz - Distortion 
 Mix Master-buss Processing, Automation, & Endgame 
 Quick Mix 5 
 How to work through it. Read the pages in the order they are listed, then do the assignment, then take the quiz. The quiz assumes you have already done the assignment, not the other way round.

pages.title: Master-Buss Processing and Endgame: Procedure Guide
pages.text:
Master-Buss Processing and Endgame: Procedure Guide 
 Master-Buss Processing and Endgame: Procedure Guide
 Follow this in order. Each step assumes the one before it is complete. If a step will not work, the cause is almost always something skipped earlier, not the step you are on.
 Figure 1. Channel Strip, showing the EQ curve and the dynamics graph in one window. On a master buss every move here should be small enough to argue for.
 Use this self-contained guide before completing the assignment work in this module. It explains the operating workflow; the corresponding assignment provides the required project-specific settings and submission evidence.
 Step-by-Step Workflow
 Finish corrective work on individual tracks before adding processing to the master bus.
 Insert master-bus processing in a deliberate order and make small, level-matched changes. Leave headroom for the final bounce.
 Use automation to support musical transitions, then listen from start to finish for level jumps, clicks, clipped peaks, and unintended changes.
 Make the required bounce from an exact timeline selection, re-import it, and listen to the delivered file before submission.
 Reference: Apply the current Avid Pro Tools Reference Guide procedures that correspond to the tools used here. Keep an untouched playlist or session version before making destructive edits. 
 This page is self-contained and does not rely on links to other Canvas pages.
 Save before and after. Save the session before you start and again when you finish, with a version number in the name. It costs two seconds and it is the only undo that survives a crash.

pages.title: Master-Buss Processing and Endgame: Knowing When to Stop
pages.text:
Master-Buss Processing and Endgame: Knowing When to Stop 
 Master-Buss Processing and Endgame: Knowing When to Stop
 The master buss is not where a mix gets fixed. If the mix needs 4 dB of master buss EQ, the problem is on a channel. Go back and find it. Master buss processing is for the last few percent, after the mix already works.
 Figure 1. Channel Strip, showing the EQ curve and the dynamics graph in one window. On a master buss every move here should be small enough to argue for.
 These are the controls this module turns on. Know what each one does before you decide what to set it to.
 Each control and what it does
 Control What it does 
 Master fader Post everything. Leave it at unity and control level upstream. 
 Buss compression Small amounts. 1 to 2 dB of gain reduction on the mix buss is a lot. 
 Buss EQ Broad moves only. If you need a narrow cut on the master, it belongs on a track. 
 Limiting For control, not for loudness, at this stage. Mastering is a different job with different ears. 
 Headroom on delivery Leave the peaks under 0 dBFS. What you deliver is not what a streaming service will play back. 
 Leave headroom on delivery. Print with peaks around -6 dBFS and no limiter on the master unless the assignment asks for one. Mastering needs room to work, and a mix squashed flat gives it none.
 How to know you are done. You are done when your next three moves are all under 1 dB and you cannot say which one helped. Bounce it, leave it a day, and listen once in the car. If you still want to change something, it will be obvious in the first ten seconds.

pages.title: Master-Buss Processing & Endgame: Common Mistakes and How to Hear Them
pages.text:
Master-Buss Processing & Endgame: Common Mistakes and How to Hear Them 
 Master-Buss Processing & Endgame: Common Mistakes and How to Hear Them
 These are the errors that cost marks. Every item below has shown up in real student submissions in this course. Read them before you submit, not after you get the grade back.
 Figure 1. Headroom against a mix pushed into the ceiling. What you deliver is not what a streaming service plays back.
 Every one of these is a mistake that gets made in this room every semester. The middle column is the part worth memorizing: what the mistake sounds like is how you catch it in your own work.
 Each mistake, the sound that gives it away, and what to do instead
 The mistake What you hear What to do instead 
 Mix buss processing added at the end Every balance decision was made without it, and adding it undoes them. Put it on early and mix into it, or leave it off. 
 Chasing loudness on the master The mix is loud, flat and tiring, and streaming will turn it down anyway. Mix for dynamics. Loudness normalization means the loud mix wins nothing. 
 Not knowing when it is done Endless revisions, each one different and none better. Leave it overnight. If you cannot name what is wrong the next morning, it is finished. 
 Hearing it is the skill. Each mistake has a listening cue attached. Learn the cue and you stop needing the checklist.

items.stem: Two students log in to the same lab Mac with their own accounts. Student A builds a custom Pro Tools key command set. Student B opens Pro Tools and does not see it, but both can load the same AAX plug-ins. Why?
options: Key commands are per user in ~/Library; AAX plug-ins are shared in /Library
Key commands are saved inside the session file, which Student B has not opened
Key commands live in /System, which only an admin account can load
Student B's Pro Tools install is damaged and needs reinstalling
key: Key commands are per user in ~/Library; AAX plug-ins are shared in /Library
items.title: Question

items.stem: Your rough mix feels lopsided and has no solid middle, and you find several tracks panned off center. Which of these should go back to the center? (mark all that apply)
options: Kick
Snare
Bass
Lead vocal
Doubled rhythm guitar pair
Stereo synth pad
Tambourine
Backing vocal stack
key: Kick
Snare
Bass
Lead vocal
items.title: Question

items.stem: Dynamic effects serve 2 main purposes.  What are they? (Choose all that apply)
options: Envelope shapers
Dynamic range manipulators
Reverberators
Pitch correctors
key: Envelope shapers
Dynamic range manipulators
items.title: M08: Dynamic Effects (classic)

items.stem: What is the primary reason for starting with a blank slate when mixing other people's musical material?
options: To save time by using the client's rough-mix setup
To bring a fresh perspective to the production
To ensure compatibility with the client's mixing system
To avoid using any effects or processing
key: To bring a fresh perspective to the production
items.title: Quiz 03 - Essential Groundwork

items.stem: Every join in your vocal comp has a small click or a doubled consonant. What is the fix?
options: Move each edit just before the transient, then crossfade
Place each edit exactly on the transient so takes line up
Remove the crossfades so the joins are sample accurate
Lower the clip gain on each comped phrase
key: Move each edit just before the transient, then crossfade
items.title: Question

items.stem: Why is it recommended to tighten the timing of each layer one at a time?
options: To save time by editing all layers together
To ensure each layer fits the groove in isolation
To avoid phase incoherence
To make the process more challenging
key: To ensure each layer fits the groove in isolation
items.title: Quiz 05: Timing and Tuning

items.stem: What is the key to fluent balancing according to the text?
options: Letting the faders set the agenda
Ignoring fader instability
Using as many plug-ins as possible
Rebuilding the plugin structure multiple times
key: Letting the faders set the agenda
items.title: Quiz 11_Balancing and Reverb

items.stem: Your vocal delay has piled up so many repeats that it blurs into the next line. Which control is the most direct fix?
options: Lower the feedback
Raise the feedback
Raise the Mix control
Add pre-delay
key: Lower the feedback
items.title: Question

items.stem: A student's room sounds boomy and their mixes carry the wrong amount of low end on other systems. Which treatment moves does the reading recommend first? (mark all that apply)
options: Broadband absorbers with real depth
Bass traps in the corners
Thin foam panels across the walls
Moving the mix position back against the rear wall
key: Broadband absorbers with real depth
Bass traps in the corners
items.title: Question

items.stem: What is an EQ? (mark all that apply)
options: A frequency-specific volume knob.
A device that lets you control the dynamic range of a signal
A device that uses changes in phase to change the volume of specific frequencies
key: A frequency-specific volume knob.
A device that uses changes in phase to change the volume of specific frequencies
items.title: Quiz_09_Spectral Effects

items.stem: Aliasing is:  (mark all that apply)
options: A type of distortion caused by digitally recording a signal at a lower sample rate than it should be
A good way to make a signal sound like an old video game
Creates a metallic edge to a sound
Adds information to the signal that is harmonically related to the original signal
key: A type of distortion caused by digitally recording a signal at a lower sample rate than it should be
A good way to make a signal sound like an old video game
Creates a metallic edge to a sound
items.title: Quiz_13_Distortion

items.stem: You drag an app to the Trash, reinstall it a month later, and it opens with all your old settings and presets. Why?
options: Deleting the app left its files in ~/Library behind
The settings live inside the .app bundle you reinstalled
A registry entry kept the settings, as on Windows
The settings are in /System, which the Trash cannot touch
key: Deleting the app left its files in ~/Library behind
items.title: Question

items.stem: Match the concept to the corresponding question:
options: What is important right now?
Can I hear everything?
Is my audience still listening?
Where was the song recorded?
What does the audience care about?
Who shows the most dedication?
Can the audience join in the recording?
items.title: M07: Mixing with Focus and Balance (classic)

items.stem: After you insert a compressor on the kick, the kick loses its front end and the mix loses punch. What should you change first?
options: Slow the attack so the transient gets through before gain reduction starts
Speed up the attack so the compressor catches the transient sooner
Raise the ratio to 10:1
Add makeup gain until the kick is as loud as before
key: Slow the attack so the transient gets through before gain reduction starts
items.title: Question

items.stem: You have been adjusting a mix for an hour. Your last three moves were all under 1 dB and you cannot say which one helped. What should you do?
options: Bounce it, leave it a day, then listen once in the car
Add a limiter on the master buss to finish it
Keep making small moves until one clearly helps
Solo each track in turn and look for problems
key: Bounce it, leave it a day, then listen once in the car
items.title: Question

items.stem: After comping, a lead vocal sounds inhuman and the phrases run together. What did the student most likely do?
options: Cut out the breaths between phrases
Put each edit right on a transient
Left the joins without crossfades
Comped each line from a different take
key: Cut out the breaths between phrases
items.title: Question

items.stem: A bass part felt good before your timing pass. After you tightened it, it feels stiff and you cannot say why. What is the most likely cause?
options: The push or drag you removed was deliberate feel
The Elastic Audio algorithm was set to Monophonic
The quantize strength was left below 100 percent
The timing edits were left without crossfades
key: The push or drag you removed was deliberate feel
items.title: Question

items.stem: What should be your first priority when balancing a mix?
options: Achieving a solid balance without artifacts
Using the loudest settings
Ensuring each instrument sounds stunning
Adding as many tracks as possible
key: Achieving a solid balance without artifacts
items.title: Quiz 11_Balancing and Reverb

items.stem: What are the benefits of using delay effects over reverb in audio mixing?
options: Delay effects provide more control over timing and rhythm.
Delay effects are easier to use than reverb.
Delay effects create a more natural sound environment.
Delay effects are more suitable for live performances.
key: Delay effects provide more control over timing and rhythm.
items.title: Quiz 12_Delay and Stereo Enhancements

items.stem: At your mix position the kick and bass change noticeably when you lean forward six inches. What should you do before trusting low-end decisions? (mark all that apply)
options: Fix the listening position
Check the low end on another system
EQ the bass until it sounds right at the mix position
Add thin foam to the side walls
key: Fix the listening position
Check the low end on another system
items.title: Question

items.stem: In the full mix the cymbals cover the vocal's upper range, but the vocal sounds fine soloed. Which move best addresses this?
options: Cut the cymbals where the vocal lives, in the full mix
Boost the vocal's top end with the vocal soloed
Cut the vocal's upper range so it stops fighting the cymbals
Put a fast-attack compressor on the vocal
key: Cut the cymbals where the vocal lives, in the full mix
items.title: Question

items.stem: What is a subharmonic synthesizer?
options: An effect that adds low frequency energy to a signal that is still musically related to the unprocessed sound
An effect that adds low frequency information to a signal similar to an EQ boost
An effect that adds high frequency information to a signal that psychoacoustically tricks your brain into thinking a pitch is lower than it actually is
key: An effect that adds low frequency energy to a signal that is still musically related to the unprocessed sound
items.title: Quiz_13_Distortion

items.stem: A classmate logged in as jlee says the practice session is at ~/Documents/Mix01. Which absolute path does that point to?
options: /Users/jlee/Documents/Mix01
/Documents/Mix01
/Library/Documents/Mix01
/System/Users/jlee/Documents/Mix01
key: /Users/jlee/Documents/Mix01
items.title: Question

items.stem: On a snare compressor, the gain reduction meter never returns to zero between hits. What does this tell you?
options: The release is too slow
The release is too fast
The attack is too slow
The makeup gain is too high
key: The release is too slow
items.title: Question

items.stem: What is one benefit of bouncing MIDI tracks to audio early in the mixing process?
options: It increases CPU load
It allows for endless tinkering with synth settings
It reduces CPU load and avoids synchronization issues
It makes MIDI instruments respond differently with each play-through
key: It reduces CPU load and avoids synchronization issues
items.title: Quiz 03 - Essential Groundwork

items.stem: You are comping a percussive muted guitar part and a sustained string pad. How should your crossfade lengths differ?
options: Short fades at the guitar joins, longer fades in the pad
Long fades on the guitar, short fades on the pad
The same long fade everywhere so nothing clicks
No fades on the pad, since it has no transients to click
key: Short fades at the guitar joins, longer fades in the pad
items.title: Question

items.stem: You quantize a drummer's hi-hat at 100 percent strength and it now sounds dead on the grid and lifeless. What should you try?
options: Requantize at about 50 to 70 percent strength
Keep 100 percent and switch the algorithm to Polyphonic
Keep 100 percent and add crossfades at every edit
Quantize the rest of the kit at 100 percent to match
key: Requantize at about 50 to 70 percent strength
items.title: Question

items.stem: What is confirmation bias in the context of audio mixing?
options: The tendency to perceive things as we expect them to be.
The tendency to always trust new technology.
The tendency to perceive things as they actually are.
The tendency to ignore all biases.
key: The tendency to perceive things as we expect them to be.
items.title: Quiz 11_Balancing and Reverb

items.stem: Describe the difference between a send-return effect configuration and an insert setup when using delay effects.
options: A send-return configuration allows for parallel processing of the delay effect, while an insert setup processes the effect in series with the original signal.
Both configurations process the effect in series with the original signal.
A send-return configuration processes the effect in series with the original signal, while an insert setup allows for parallel processing of the delay effect.
Both configurations allow for parallel processing of the delay effect.
key: A send-return configuration allows for parallel processing of the delay effect, while an insert setup processes the effect in series with the original signal.
items.title: Quiz 12_Delay and Stereo Enhancements

items.stem: Headphones are very good at the following (mark all that apply):
options: Helping you hear detail that is normally lost in loudspeakers
Helping you hear panning and stereo image
Helping you hear errors, clicks, pops, short dropouts, etc.
Helping you predict how a mix will sound on loudspeakers
key: Helping you hear detail that is normally lost in loudspeakers
Helping you hear panning and stereo image
Helping you hear errors, clicks, pops, short dropouts, etc.
items.title: Quiz_01_Mix Room Setup

items.stem: Your audio interface driver installed a helper in /Library/LaunchDaemons. You run launchctl list in Terminal as yourself and do not see it. Why?
options: Daemons run as root, so they only appear with sudo launchctl list
The driver failed to install and must be reinstalled
Daemons start only after you log in, so you must log out and back in
launchctl list shows only Apple's own processes
key: Daemons run as root, so they only appear with sudo launchctl list
items.title: Question

items.stem: A vocal compressor has its threshold at -20 dBFS, a 4:1 ratio, a hard knee and no makeup gain. A peak enters at -8 dBFS. Where does that peak leave the compressor?
options: -17 dBFS
-11 dBFS
-8 dBFS
-20 dBFS
key: -17 dBFS
items.title: Question

items.stem: A student's Audio Files folder is full of files named Audio 1-01 through Audio 47-03, even though every track in the session now has a proper name. What caused this?
options: The tracks were named after recording, not before
The session was saved without a version number
The comped clips were never consolidated
Pro Tools renames files only when the session closes
key: The tracks were named after recording, not before
items.title: Question

items.stem: What is one method suggested to combat confirmation bias in audio mixing?
options: Use a plug-in's bypass button and toggle it without looking.
Only rely on meters.
Avoid using any software tools.
Always trust your initial settings.
key: Use a plug-in's bypass button and toggle it without looking.
items.title: Quiz 11_Balancing and Reverb

items.stem: What is the advantage of making delays sonically different to the dry tracks?
options: It creates a more immersive sound experience.
It reduces the overall volume of the track.
It makes the track sound more monotonous.
It eliminates the need for any effects.
key: It creates a more immersive sound experience.
items.title: Quiz 12_Delay and Stereo Enhancements

items.stem: When treating your mixing space, try to prevent ____________________ whenever possible.
options: first reflections
absorption
diffusion
key: first reflections
items.title: Quiz_01_Mix Room Setup

items.stem: A license helper starts only when you log in to your own account and does not run for other accounts on the same Mac. Where would you look for its Launch Agent .plist?
options: ~/Library/LaunchAgents
/Library/LaunchAgents
/Library/LaunchDaemons
/System/Library/LaunchAgents
key: ~/Library/LaunchAgents
items.title: Question

items.stem: Which control on a compressor specifies the level above which the signal is considered too loud?
options: Threshold
Attack
Input gain
Output level
key: Threshold
items.title: M08: Dynamic Effects (classic)

items.stem: You reopen your own session after two weeks and spend minutes hunting for the bass and vocal tracks before every move. Which prep step would have prevented this?
options: Color coding and a consistent track order set before mixing
Saving the session with a version number in its name
Setting every fader to unity before the first pass
Raising clip gain on the tracks you use most
key: Color coding and a consistent track order set before mixing
items.title: Question

items.stem: You are about to build a lead vocal comp from five takes. What should you do first so the original performance stays available?
options: Duplicate the source playlist before auditioning takes
Consolidate all five takes into one clip
Delete the weakest takes to reduce clutter
Add crossfades to every take before choosing phrases
key: Duplicate the source playlist before auditioning takes
items.title: Question

items.stem: What is a common oversight in timing correction for small-studio engineers?
options: Ignoring the timing of rhythm guitars
Over-editing the drum parts
Neglecting the timing of lead vocals
Focusing too much on bass timing
key: Neglecting the timing of lead vocals
items.title: Quiz 05: Timing and Tuning

items.stem: You A/B an EQ move on a vocal. The EQ version sounds better, but it is also about 2 dB louder than the bypassed version. What should you do before deciding?
options: Level-match the bypassed and active states, then compare again
Keep the EQ, since louder and better usually go together
Raise the bypassed track fader by 6 dB and compare
Solo the vocal so the comparison is not affected by the mix
key: Level-match the bypassed and active states, then compare again
items.title: Question

items.stem: What is a common problem when using a single 50 to 100ms short 'slapback' delay with little or no feedback?
options: It creates a muddy sound
It results in a thin sound
It causes phase cancellation
It introduces unwanted distortion
key: It creates a muddy sound
items.title: Quiz 12_Delay and Stereo Enhancements

items.stem: A plug-in with a valid license suddenly refuses to authorize after you log in to the lab Mac. What should you check first?
options: Its Launch Agent or Launch Daemon
The Playback Engine buffer size
The session sample rate in the Dashboard
The macOS Sound output device
key: Its Launch Agent or Launch Daemon
items.title: Question

items.stem: Your vocal peaks reach about -10 dBFS. On the compressor, the threshold is set to -4 dB and the gain reduction meter never moves. Why?
options: The threshold is above every peak, so no signal crosses it
The ratio is set too high to register on the meter
The attack is too fast for the meter to show
The makeup gain is set to 0 dB
key: The threshold is above every peak, so no signal crosses it
items.title: Question

items.stem: Halfway through a mix you notice the session was created at 44.1 kHz, but the project spec requires a 48 kHz session. What does changing the session sample rate now involve?
options: Converting every audio file in the session to the new rate
Changing one Dashboard setting; the files follow on their own
Changing the Playback Engine rate; the files never need converting
Nothing, because audio files do not store a sample rate
key: Converting every audio file in the session to the new rate
items.title: Question

items.stem: Your vocal comp has no clicks and every join is crossfaded, but it sounds musically dead. What is the most likely cause?
options: Takes were chosen by eye from the waveforms
The breaths were left in between phrases
Every join was crossfaded
Edits sat in the quiet before each transient
key: Takes were chosen by eye from the waveforms
items.title: Question

items.stem: A rhythm guitar feels slightly behind the beat in the chorus. Before you start moving transients, what should you do?
options: Check against the kick whether the drag is deliberate
Quantize it at 100 percent so it can never drift again
Line each transient up with the grid by eye
Set Elastic Audio to Rhythmic for the strums
key: Check against the kick whether the drag is deliberate
items.title: Question

items.stem: Your vocal delay is set exactly to an eighth note from the session tempo, yet the repeats feel rhythmically wrong against the groove. What does the reading recommend?
options: Tap it in against the track, even off the grid
Add feedback until the repeats feel in time
Line the repeats up with the grid lines by eye
Recalculate the eighth note in ms from the tempo
key: Tap it in against the track, even off the grid
items.title: Question

items.stem: You slowed the tracking speed on your MacBook trackpad at home for fine automation edits. In the lab, with an external mouse, the pointer is still too fast. Why?
options: The mouse and the trackpad each have their own separate speed setting
Pro Tools overrides macOS tracking speed in the Edit window
Tracking speed only applies after the Mac restarts
Natural scrolling is turned off on the lab Mac
key: The mouse and the trackpad each have their own separate speed setting
items.title: Question

items.stem: What is usually a characteristic of compressors with Input Gain controls?
options: They have a fixed threshold level
They add distortion to the sound
They reduce the signal's overall level
They increase the dynamic range
key: They have a fixed threshold level
items.title: M08: Dynamic Effects (classic)

items.stem: What is one downside of recording numerous full "top to tail" takes?
options: It requires less concentration from the musician
It demands more concentration and endurance from the musician
It is quicker than other methods
It results in fewer expressive moments
key: It demands more concentration and endurance from the musician
items.title: Quiz 04 - Comping and Arranging

items.stem: After tightening a drum loop with Elastic Audio, the hits flam and smear. What is the most likely cause?
options: The Elastic Audio algorithm does not suit the source
The quantize strength was left below 100 percent
The loop was not consolidated before editing
The loop's sample rate does not match the session
key: The Elastic Audio algorithm does not suit the source
items.title: Question

items.stem: A mono rhythm guitar needs to sound wider, and the mix will be heard on phones and laptops. Which approach gives width that mostly survives a mono sum?
options: A 15 to 30 ms delay on one side
A stereo imager that phase-inverts the sides
More level on one side than the other
A duplicate of the track panned hard opposite
key: A 15 to 30 ms delay on one side
items.title: Question

items.stem: On a lab MacBook, clips keep getting selected by accident whenever you rest a finger lightly on the trackpad while editing. Which setting do you turn off?
options: Tap to Click
Force Click
Natural scrolling
Tracking speed
key: Tap to Click
items.title: Question

items.stem: One word in a vocal line jumps out far louder than the rest and the compressor clamps hard on it. What does the reading recommend doing first?
options: Lower that word with clip gain before the compressor
Ride the master fader down during that word
Raise the ratio to 20:1 for the whole vocal
Add makeup gain until the quiet words match the loud one
key: Lower that word with clip gain before the compressor
items.title: Question

items.stem: Why is it beneficial to have a generic session layout for each mix project?
options: It allows for more creative thinking during the mix
It ensures all projects sound the same
It makes the mixing process more complex
It reduces the need for any mixing decisions
key: It allows for more creative thinking during the mix
items.title: Quiz 03 - Essential Groundwork

items.stem: What is a disadvantage of recording a single track one phrase at a time?
options: It maintains musical flow
It can feel disjointed emotionally
It is more efficient
It requires less editing

options: Loop the phrase and cycle the lanes, listening in context
Judge each take on its own with the rest of the band muted
Pick the take whose waveform looks the most even
Pick the loudest take so it cuts through the mix
key: Loop the phrase and cycle the lanes, listening in context

items.stem: An acoustic guitar adds low rumble under the bass, energy the part never needed. Which filter shape removes it?
options: A high-pass filter on the guitar
A low-pass filter on the guitar
A narrow bell boost on the bass to lift it clear
A high shelf boost on the guitar
key: A high-pass filter on the guitar
items.title: Question

items.stem: Delays are often preferred over reverbs for modern music styles because:
options: they create a sense of space without cluttering the mix.
they are more affordable.
they are easier to use.
they are more traditional.
key: they create a sense of space without cluttering the mix.
items.title: Quiz 12_Delay and Stereo Enhancements

items.stem: A student says zooming in the Pro Tools Edit window feels backwards on a lab Mac. What should you check first?
options: The macOS scroll direction setting
The Pro Tools Playback Engine device
The mouse tracking speed setting
Whether Pro Tools needs reinstalling
key: The macOS scroll direction setting

items.stem: Why might electric guitarists rarely require compression?
options: They naturally produce a consistent sound level.
They are always playing in small studios.
They use other effects that replace the need for compression.
They play chords
key: They naturally produce a consistent sound level.
items.title: M08: Dynamic Effects (classic)

items.stem: During session prep you want to jump instantly to each chorus and bridge while mixing. What should you set up?

 What each kind of work looks like when it is handed in

pages.title: Pro Tools Fundamentals: Lab 01 Manual Procedure Guide
pages.text:
Pro Tools Fundamentals: Lab 01 Manual Procedure Guide 
 Pro Tools Fundamentals: Lab 01 Manual Procedure Guide
 Follow this in order. Each step assumes the one before it is complete. If a step will not work, the cause is almost always something skipped earlier, not the step you are on.
 Use this guide to practice the workflow before starting the timed assignment. It explains the Pro Tools operations required by the assignment; the assignment page remains the source for the required track names, file name, timing, and submission.
 1. Build the session before importing
 Create a local BWF session at 48 kHz and 24-bit with a stereo mix path, then save it to the required location using the DAPR naming convention.
 Create the required mono and stereo audio tracks. Name them before importing so each audio file has a clear destination.
 Set the main counter and ruler display to Bars and Beats. Use Samples as the time scale when making sample-accurate selections for tempo mapping.
 2. Import and place audio
 Choose File > Import > Audio , locate the provided lab files, and add them to the Clip List. Choose the option that copies them into the session Audio Files folder.
 Audition unfamiliar clips from the Clip List when needed. Expand stereo files if you need to place only the left or right channel on a mono track.
 Drag each clip from the Clip List to its named track at the beginning of the session. Check that mono sources are on mono tracks and stereo sources are on stereo tracks.
 3. Identify the beat and verify the tempo map
 Find a clear downbeat and make a precise sample-based selection from that downbeat to a known later bar boundary. A longer accurate selection reduces rounding error.
 Select the audio with the Time Grabber, then choose Event > Identify Beat .
 In the Bar|Beat Markers dialog, enter the musical location at the beginning and end of the selection. For example, a verified one-bar selection runs from 1|1|000 to 2|1|000 ; a four-bar selection runs from 1|1|000 to 5|1|000 .
 Confirm the correct meter, apply the result, then loop playback to make sure the Bars and Beats ruler stays aligned with the music. Correct the selection before moving on if the grid drifts.
 Figure 1. Bar and Beat Markers from the Pro Tools 2026.4.1 Reference Guide. 
 4. Make the required grid edit
 Set the Grid value to one-quarter note and enable Grid mode.
 At the required bar boundary, use the Selector to make the cut across the required clips.
 Move the material after the cut exactly one measure to the right. Copy the required tambourine measure into the empty bar.
 Create short fades or crossfades at every edit. Zoom in and listen across each cut before continuing.
 5. Pan, automate, and bounce
 Set the required pan positions in the Mix window.
 Show Volume automation on the required track. Add breakpoints at the song start and at the specified measure, then shape the fade so it begins fully down and reaches 0 dB at the required point.
 Make a timeline selection from the beginning through the required end bar. Choose File > Bounce Mix , select the required BWF, PCM, interleaved, bit-depth, sample-rate, and offline settings, and enable Import After Bounce.
 After the bounce returns to the session, listen to the imported file and verify that it starts, ends, and plays correctly.
 Manual reference: Avid Pro Tools Reference Guide 2026.4.1, the reading for this module, "Identify Beat Command," manual pages 1149-1150. The guide also covers Clip List importing, grid editing, automation, and Bounce Mix in its relevant workflow chapters. 
 This page is self-contained and does not rely on links to other Canvas pages.
 Save before and after. Save the session before you start and again when you finish, with a version number in the name. It costs two seconds and it is the only undo that survives a crash.

pages.title: macOS: P1: Getting Around Your Mac
pages.text:
macOS: P1: Getting Around Your Mac 
 macOS: P1: Getting Around Your Mac
 Pro Tools sits on top of macOS, and macOS has its own set of keyboard modifiers, hidden folders, and system settings that change how Pro Tools behaves. This page walks you through the five pieces of Mac navigation every mixer needs: Finder modifier keys, the Function key toggle, hiding background windows, telling Sound Preferences apart from Pro Tools Preferences, and finding the Library folder where your plug-ins and background helper processes actually live.
 Goals
 Use Finder modifier keys to select, copy, and move files with precision.
 Set the Function key toggle so your F-keys work as Pro Tools key commands, not media controls.
 Hide every window except your active app with a single shortcut.
 Explain the difference between macOS Sound Preferences and the Pro Tools Playback Engine.
 Locate your Library folder, your installed plug-ins, and your Launch Agents and Launch Daemons.
 Finder Modifier Keys
 Every modifier key changes what a click or a drag does in Finder. Learn these five and file management stops being guesswork.
 Click 
 - selects one file and deselects everything else. 
 Shift + Click 
 - selects every file between your last click and this one. 
 Command + Click 
 - adds or removes individual files from the selection without touching the rest. 
 Option + Drag 
 - copies the file to the destination instead of moving it. Use this when dragging within the same drive. 
 Command + Drag 
 - forces a move instead of a copy. Use this when dragging between two different drives, since Finder copies across drives by default. 
 Note: 
 Control + Click opens the same contextual menu as a right-click. Every Mac trackpad and mouse supports this even without a right-click button configured. 
 The Function Key Toggle
 Pro Tools puts key commands on F1 through F12. macOS ships with those same keys set to control volume, brightness, and media playback instead. Set the toggle below once, and your F-keys work directly in Pro Tools.
 Without this setting, your F-keys turn into media keys. 
 Pressing F1 lowers your screen brightness instead of triggering the Pro Tools command mapped to it. To get the true F-key signal through without changing this setting, you would have to hold Fn every single time - that is not workable mid-session. 
 Open System Settings .
 Click Keyboard in the sidebar.
 Click Keyboard Shortcuts .
 Select Function Keys in the left-hand list.
 Check Use F1, F2, etc. keys as standard function keys .
 Close System Settings.
 The Function Keys panel with the toggle switched on.
 Tip: 
 With this setting on, the two functions swap places. Your F-keys now send standard F1-F12 signals to Pro Tools directly. Hold Fn at the same time as an F-key to get the media function (volume, brightness, play/pause) back. 
 Hide Other Windows
 A mix session fills your screen with plugin windows, browsers, and Finder windows. One shortcut clears everything except your active app.
 Command + H 
 - hides the windows of the app you are currently in. 
 Command + Option + H 
 - hides every other open app and leaves only your active app's windows on screen. 
 Note: 
 Find the same command in the menu bar under the app name's menu, listed as Hide Others . 
 Sound Preferences vs. Pro Tools Preferences
 macOS Sound settings and the Pro Tools Playback Engine are two completely separate audio paths. Changing one does not change the other.
 These two settings control different things: 
 System Settings > Sound sets the device macOS uses for system alerts, notifications, and any non-Pro-Tools audio, such as a browser tab.
 Pro Tools > Setup > Playback Engine sets the audio interface Pro Tools uses for your session. This is independent of the macOS Sound setting.
 Set your interface in Playback Engine for every Pro Tools session. The macOS Sound output can stay on the Mac's built-in speakers for everything else - the two settings will not conflict.
 The macOS Sound pane's Output list on a real production Mac - notice how many virtual devices show up here (Pro Tools Audio Bridge, Dolby Audio Bridge, and more) alongside the actual hardware. None of these are selected in Playback Engine automatically just because they appear here.
 Library, Plug-Ins, and Launch Agents
 Your plug-ins, and the background processes that authorize them, live inside the Library folder. macOS hides this folder from you by default.
 Reveal your user Library folder: 
 In Finder, open the Go menu, hold Option , and click Library once it appears in the list. Or use Go > Go to Folder and type ~/Library . 
 /Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/ 
 - plug-ins installed for every user account on the machine (System Library). 
 ~/Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/ 
 - plug-ins installed for your user account only (User Library). 
 ~/Library/LaunchAgents and /Library/LaunchAgents 
 - background helper processes that start when a single user logs in. iLok, interface drivers, and plug-in license managers install these. 
 /Library/LaunchDaemons 
 - background processes that start at the system level, before any user logs in. These run system-wide services rather than per-user apps. 
 Tip: 
 When a plug-in or interface will not authorize, check its Launch Agent or Launch Daemon first. A stalled background helper process is the most common cause.

pages.title: macOS: P1: Mac Interface and Application Behavior
pages.text:
macOS: P1: Mac Interface and Application Behavior 
 macOS: P1: Mac Interface and Application Behavior
 Every Mac screen is built from the same handful of pieces, and every app follows the same rules for opening, closing, and switching. Once these rules click, navigating any Mac - not just this one - stops requiring guesswork.
 The Building Blocks of the Screen
 Desktop 
 - the background layer everything else sits on top of. It can hold files and folders, and shows your wallpaper. 
 Menu Bar 
 - the strip across the top of the screen. Its menus - File, Edit, and the rest - always belong to whichever app is currently active, and change the instant you switch apps. System status icons live on the right side. 
 Apple menu
